surface: The column menu's Filter by condition on a numeric column: the condition select and its option list, the value input, and OK applying the filter.

steps.note: The menu of the Price column opens. In this fixture `columns` is set, so Insert column left and right and Remove column are disabled and the keyboard skips them: the first highlighted item is `Clear column` (tree golden of this page). Unsure of that first item until a run records it. Finding: VoiceOver says nothing when the column menu opens: 9 of 9 opens on Chromium and 7 of 9 on WebKit over three runs, where the context menu in grid-core is announced. NVDA with Chromium names the menu as a table and says menu in some runs only, as it does for the context menu in grid-core.

The first Tab moves from the menu to the Filter by condition select, a listbox showing its current option, `None`. It has no accessible name of its own in the tree golden, so only the option is required. Finding: the condition select is read as `list` (NVDA, both browsers) or `list box` (VoiceOver with Chromium), with neither its name nor its current option; only VoiceOver with WebKit reads the option.

Enter opens the select's own option list (a menu of its own) with the first option highlighted. The Price column's list is None, Is empty, Is not empty, Is equal to, Is not equal to, Greater than, Greater than or equal to, Less than, Less than or equal to, Is between (the grid-level rule drops Is not between; separators between groups).
The separator after None is skipped.
The separator after Is not empty is skipped.

Enter chooses Is equal to, closes the option list and, on a 10 ms timer, moves the focus to the value input, whose name is its `Value` placeholder. Unsure: the capture may hold only the select's new caption, `Is equal to`, if the reader settles before the timer fires. VoiceOver with WebKit reads the field's name without its role.
The value to compare (Mountain Frame's price). Nothing is required: a reader echoes the typed digits.

The way to OK goes backwards on purpose: the forward Tab walk from here is seven stops (And, Or, the second select, search, Select all, Select none, OK) and this scenario stays within its step budget. Shift+Tab returns to the select, which now shows its chosen option. Finding: the condition select is read as `list` (NVDA, both browsers) or `list box` (VoiceOver with Chromium), with neither its name nor its chosen option; only VoiceOver with WebKit reads the option.

Shift+Tab from the first component gives the focus back to the menu itself with the item the loop started from highlighted again (filters-menu-focus-order.spec.ts, #10603). Unsure: that restore is the first Tab's `Clear column`; a reader may announce the menu rather than the item.
Shift+Tab from the menu wraps to the last component, the Cancel button.

Enter on OK applies Is equal to 1890 (only Mountain Frame stays) and closes the menu; the focus returns to the grid's focus cell, row 0 of the Price column, now 1890. Finding candidate: the menu closing may leave a reader on the document, as grid-core records for the context menu.
